column2: What inspired you to build that project and how long did it take?

I built a trading algo that gave me a 29% return over the year > $500 month. I applied the lessons I learned while building major trading solution like Murex and Calypso.

And now finalizing an open source development harness that I hope will be successful and will drive consulting business in AI. Check www.nomorehappypath.com

I run a niche analytics business for like $4000 MRR currently, genuinely 'vibe coded' it to try out LLM capacities (late comer on the LLM train here). I felt like the need was there and competition was weak, low tier SWE, overall really easy to take over and so I did and now I'm scaling up and expanding the product line.
It cost about 4 months of $200 claude, about $700 of proxies since launch, a very optimized bare metal hetzner server. 'Content creator' industry.

Bug bounty and security research keeps me a good bit above 500 per month...

I experienced an initial influx of positive results and rewards as I ramped up AI use initially. However, as time goes on, I expect that to trickle out at some point since everyone and their mother now has something that can hunt and find better bugs than me. so I will have to either find a better niche or do something else with my time, but for now - that is my only side project.

I quite enjoy it so I have been brainstorming ways to stay involved and contribute without getting behind the times. Any ideas are welcome. Lol.

I raw http://www.lokobee.com/ Doordash like restaurant food ordering website. We have some active restaurants. Brings in few orders per restaurant per day. But surprisingly we drive more traffic to some restaurants than uber eats. Revenue(GMV) is better than $1000 per month.

I do, a saas running for nearly 20 years.

How long is not as important as does anybody want what you are selling.

My advice is aim at something boring that people rely on everyday. Be the person who sells razor blades, so to speak.

I do, a Shopify app that helps merchants track orders across long manufacturing/fulfillment processes. I built it ages ago when I was working as manual labor at a printing company, watching everyone run around all day trying to figure out where each order was. I'd daydream about how I could improve things and make them more efficient, write my ideas down in a notebook, then go home and build it in the evening.

I think the app is something like 12 years old now, but I still work on it to this day. I'm adding a new feature to it right now, and would like to kick the Shopify dependency someday soon.
No. However I am improving the visibility of the project via multiple channels like HN, PH. My project: https://apxy.dev/

Uruky [1] has been doing €2k / month or more for the last few months (not a subscription, though).

PodBy [2] is still below €100 / month, though.

Uruky started out late last year, and was publicly released earlier this year. My wife and I couldn’t stand the bad state (of AI) search and the lack of a simpler Kagi alternative in Europe.

PodBy was recently launched under that name, but its “tech” had been powering a few sites and projects for over a year (partially Uruky, too).

[1]: https://uruky.com

[2]: https://podby.com

I have https://www.drawdb.app/ a database diagram editor. It generated a bit more than half of my 9-5 salary this month. ~3 years open-source and 3 months of building pro and now trying to figure out all the non-development parts of running it. Fingers crossed this month wasn't an outlier
For a while I worked weekends at a retail store for about $900/mo. It's not glamorous, but this is the highest percentage way get an extra $500/mo.
Thanks, guys. Very interesting to read. I’m glad that some people are earning more than 500. You’re awesome.

No. But I am continuously improving the visibility of the project so I can pitch to teams for Sponsored Ads on the site.

The project: https://agentfriendlycode.com/
